<description>
When the old entry in a collision is unreachable and hasn't connected successfully in the last 4 hours, it can only leave the collision set through the 40-minute `ADDRMAN_TEST_WINDOW` branch. Until then, if it's the only pending collision, no feeler connections are made at all.
This is a rare occurrence I ran into when I switched from dual-homed (IPv4 + Tor) to `-onlynet=ipv4`.

`ThreadOpenConnections()` repeatedly calls `SelectTriedCollision()`, which keeps returning the unreachable entry. Since its network is unreachable, the entry is skipped without making a connection. `nTries` eventually runs out without any feeler connections being made.
The same process repeats on subsequent feeler turns until `ResolveCollisions()` resolves the collision after `ADDRMAN_TEST_WINDOW` (40 minutes).

This PR passes the reachable networks to `SelectTriedCollision()`, so it only returns collisions whose to-be-evicted entry belongs to a reachable network.
If none of the pending collisions qualify, nothing is returned, and a regular feeler connection is made instead.

Another approach I considered [2](https://github.com/naiyoma/bitcoin/pull/25) is to overwrite unreachable tried entries involved in a collision directly in `ResolveCollisions()`.
</description>

<commits>
99f5a0074c addrman: add networks filter to SelectTriedCollision

If networks is non-empty, SelectTriedCollision() starts at a random
collision and returns the first one whose to-be-evicted entry is on one
of the given networks, or nothing if there is none. Skipped collisions
are kept.

fc9f536d17 net: only test tried collisions on reachable networks with feelers

Pass reachable_nets to SelectTriedCollision() so that a pending
collision that can't be tested no longer stops feeler connections:
a regular feeler is made instead until ResolveCollisions() replaces
it after ADDRMAN_TEST_WINDOW.
</commits>
